editorial:
Imagine being only 14 years old and getting kicked out by your own family, only to end up in a strict church-run home. That is exactly what happens to Wolfgang in the summer of 1968. You will feel his frustration right away as he deals with the harsh rules and the cold attitudes of the people in charge. The vibe is very heavy and serious, making you feel like you are trapped right there with him in the middle of nowhere. It is a story about a kid who refuses to let a bleak environment break his spirit, and you will find yourself rooting for him from the very first scene.

The acting is really solid and makes the pain feel real. While the story moves a bit slowly at times, the build-up makes the moments of rebellion feel much more satisfying. You might find some parts too sad, but the emotional payoff is worth it. If you enjoy stories about overcoming the odds, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, Wolfgang finally finds the strength to break away from the institution's grip. After facing constant pressure to conform, he makes a daring move to reclaim his life. He manages to escape the confines of the sanctuary, proving that his will to be free was stronger than the rules. The movie wraps up with him leaving the bog behind, showing that he survived the trauma and finally found a path to a new beginning.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful stories about survival and freedom.
